name: Resend
look: Pure black with a serif-led display, low-opacity accent glows used only as atmosphere, and a small white button as the brightest pixel.

hero.title: Email reimagined
hero.sub: A transactional email API built by people who have debugged a deliverability problem at two in the morning. React components for templates, and logs that tell you what actually happened.

features.title: Deliverability is the product
features.sub: Sending an email is easy. Landing in the inbox, and knowing when you did not, is the hard part.

items.title: React templates
items.body: Write emails as React components with a preview server. No table layouts and no nested font tags.

items.title: Domain setup
items.body: SPF, DKIM and DMARC configured with a checker that tells you exactly what is wrong.

items.title: Real logs
items.body: Every message with its delivery events — accepted, delivered, bounced, complained — and the provider's reason.

items.title: Dedicated IPs
items.body: Warm-up handled automatically, with reputation monitored per IP.

items.title: Webhooks
items.body: Delivery events pushed to you, signed, with replay for the last thirty days.

items.title: Broadcasts
items.body: Marketing sends on the same infrastructure, kept on a separate reputation pool.

showcases.title: We tell you when it bounced, and why
showcases.body: Every message carries its full delivery event history including the receiving server's own reason string. When something lands in spam you get a diagnosis rather than a dashboard number.

showcases.title: Emails as React components
showcases.body: A component library and preview server for email, so templates are reviewed in a pull request like the rest of your code, rather than edited in a drag-and-drop tool nobody has access to.
points: React components with a preview server

testimonial.quote: The first time an email bounced it told me the receiving server's exact reason string. I had spent two years with a provider that just said 'failed'.
testimonial.name: Owen Trent

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: Free to 3,000 a month, then priced per thousand.

items.q: Do I need a dedicated IP?
items.a: Below roughly a hundred thousand a month, no — shared pools are well maintained and usually deliver better. Above that a dedicated IP with managed warm-up makes sense.
Thirty days of full event history on every plan including free, with the receiving server's reason string preserved rather than summarised.

items.q: Can I use my own domain?
items.a: Yes, and you should. The setup flow checks SPF, DKIM and DMARC and tells you precisely which record is wrong rather than saying verification failed.
Yes, on separate reputation pools, so a broadcast campaign cannot damage delivery of your password reset emails.

cta.title: Send your first email
cta.sub: Three thousand a month free, and full event logs from the start.

notes: Pure black on every public page, with off-white text carrying the whole read.
The type system is serif-led: a display serif at hero scale, a sans for marketing body, and a mono for code.
Six accent colours exist only as low-opacity atmospheric washes. None of them ever becomes a button or a solid surface.
Translucent white borders replace shadows entirely — there is no drop-shadow elevation language in this system.
The primary button is a small white rectangle with black text, deliberately the brightest pixel on the page and the single visual anchor.
